results.result: A complete serial EM reconstruction of a 3-day-old Platynereis larva was performed, identifying 9162 cells with somas and generating 5.66 million skeleton nodes with 28,717 presynaptic and 27,538 postsynaptic sites. Approximately 15-19% of nodes and synaptic sites could not be assigned to cells with somas and remain as fragments.
results.evaluation: Claims C1-C5 provide comprehensive quantitative data from the reconstruction with explicit numbers for cells, nodes, and synaptic sites. The acknowledgment of unassigned fragments (C4-C5) demonstrates methodological transparency. The data are internally consistent and represent direct observations from the EM volume.

results.result: The Platynereis larval nervous system consists of an anterior brain connected to a paired ventral nerve cord (VNC) via circumesophageal connectives, with the trunk organized into five segments. The VNC shows organized neuropil architecture with sensory neurons projecting ipsilaterally in ventro-lateral bundles, interneurons with ipsi- or contralateral projections, and motoneurons being the only class with peripheral projections concentrated dorsally.
results.evaluation: Claims C6-C12 describe the gross anatomical organization of the nervous system with consistent references to figures. The descriptions are based on direct EM observations and represent standard neuroanatomical characterization. The spatial organization of different neuron classes is clearly documented.

results.result: Neurons show quantifiable morphological properties with median cable lengths of 97.1 µm (varying by neuron type), median of 8 presynaptic and 6 postsynaptic sites, and strong correlations (r>0.7) between cable length and synapse numbers. Most neurons are unipolar with limited branching, and the ratio of pre- to postsynaptic sites distinguishes neuron classes.
results.evaluation: Claims C13-C19 provide quantitative morphological data with specific measurements and statistical correlations. The Pearson correlation coefficients >0.7 (C18) support the scaling relationships. The data are internally consistent and represent standard morphometric analyses of reconstructed neurons.

results.result: Neurons generally lack primary cilia, but sensory neurons are bipolar with 0-5 sensory cilia showing different specializations. Interneurons are unipolar or pseudo-unipolar, ciliomotor neurons have two motor axons, and other motoneurons are unipolar.
results.evaluation: Claims C20-C24 describe ultrastructural features of different neuron classes with citations to prior work (C21, C23). The descriptions are based on EM observations and are consistent with established neuronal morphology. The characterizations are straightforward and well-supported.

results.result: The synaptic connectome contains 2675 nodes connected by 14,066 directed edges formed by 26,881 synapses, representing a sparse network (density=0.00197). Source nodes are predominantly sensory neurons, sink nodes are mostly effector cells, and high-degree nodes include ciliomotor neurons and specific motoneurons.
results.evaluation: Claims C25-C30 provide network-level statistics derived from the reconstruction. The graph density calculation and node classifications are standard network analyses. The identification of high-degree nodes is supported by citations to functional studies (C29-C30), linking structure to function.

results.result: Community detection using the Leiden algorithm identified functional modules in the connectome including the visual circuit, ciliomotor network, anterior neurosecretory centre, mushroom bodies, and mechanosensory modules. These modules show stronger internal connectivity than between-module connections and correspond to functionally characterized circuits.
results.evaluation: Claims C31-C37 describe module identification using established algorithms (Leiden, C31) with citations. The functional validation of modules through citations to behavioral studies (C34, C35, C37) strengthens the biological relevance. The approach is methodologically sound for identifying functional subnetworks.

results.result: 966 neurons were classified into 202 cell types (most represented by only 2 cells), and 3128 non-neuronal cells into 92 types including diverse effector cells. Additional developing structures contain immature neurons with few synapses.
results.evaluation: Claims C38-C44 provide comprehensive cell-type classification with specific numbers. The predominance of bilaterally symmetric cell types (C39) is consistent with the organism's anatomy. The identification of developing structures (C42-C44) demonstrates thoroughness. The classifications are based on multiple criteria described in the methods.

results.result: The cell-type-level connectome contains 258 cell types (84 sensory, 82 interneurons, 34 motoneurons, 58 effectors) connected by 2410 edges and 14,640 synapses. Left-right connectivity correlation of 0.91 indicates high stereotypy, and network parameters are similar to C. elegans and C. intestinalis connectomes.
results.evaluation: Claims C45-C48 describe the grouped connectome with clear statistics. The high left-right correlation (C47) supports bilateral symmetry and reconstruction quality. The comparative analysis (C48) provides evolutionary context, though the comparison is qualitative rather than statistical.

results.result: Sensory-motor pathway analysis identified 4 sensory-motor neurons, 25 premotor sensory neurons, and a maximum path length of 5 hops from sensors to effectors. 33 sensory neurons lack paths to effectors, with 19 being neurosecretory cells.
results.evaluation: Claims C49-C53 describe circuit depth analysis with specific counts. The identification of neurosecretory cells without effector connections (C53) is biologically plausible as these cells signal through volume transmission. The analysis is straightforward graph-based path finding.

results.result: Neurotransmitter/neuropeptide phenotypes were assigned to 53 (26%) neuronal cell types, including 11 cholinergic, 3 serotonergic, 1 dopaminergic, 1 adrenergic, 4 glutamatergic types, and 38 types expressing one of 12 neuropeptides. 516 neurons contain dense core vesicles indicating peptidergic transmission.
results.evaluation: Claims C54-C57 integrate molecular data with connectome reconstruction. The ultrastructural observation of dense core vesicles (C57) corroborates the neuropeptide assignments. The relatively low percentage of assigned phenotypes (26%, C54) reflects the challenge of integrating molecular and anatomical data, but the assignments made are well-supported by citations and EM observations.

results.result: The head contains 45 sensory neuron types and 52 interneuron types, with information flowing from sensory clusters through interneurons to ciliomotor, ventral motoneuron, and descending interneuron groups. Recurrent connectivity exists between some interneuron clusters.
results.evaluation: Claims C58-C60 describe head circuit organization with specific cell type counts and connectivity patterns. The identification of recurrent connectivity (C60) is important for understanding circuit function beyond simple feedforward processing. The descriptions are based on direct connectivity analysis.

results.result: Three pairs of ventral head motoneurons (vMNs: MN1-3) form a postural control module with decussating morphology, innervating contralateral ciliated cells and muscles. Additional motor outputs include MNgland-head neurons innervating exocrine glands and several ciliomotor neurons (MC, Ser-h1, MNant, vMN) directly innervating ciliary bands.
results.evaluation: Claims C61-C66 describe specific motor circuits with citations to functional studies (C61-C62, C64-C65). The decussating morphology and contralateral innervation pattern (C62) is well-documented anatomically. The suggested link between ciliary activity and glandular secretion (C64) is appropriately presented as inference based on connectivity.

results.result: Visual integration occurs through shared postsynaptic interneurons (INR) between eye photoreceptors and eyespot PRCR1 cells. Network analysis identified MNant and vMN motoneurons with the highest presynaptic partner numbers, INRGW/INarc1/INW interneurons integrating the most inputs, and hCR neurons with the most postsynaptic cell types.
results.evaluation: Claims C67-C70 identify key integrative neurons through network analysis. The convergence of different photoreceptor types onto shared interneurons (C67) is anatomically demonstrated. The network centrality measures (C68-C70) are standard graph analyses, with the hCR neurons' broad connectivity (C70) supported by citation to functional studies.

results.result: The mushroom bodies comprise ventrolateral brain ganglia with sensory neurons (SNMB) and interneurons (INMB) classified into intrinsic (MBintrIN) and output (MBON) types. MBs receive inputs from antennae, palps, and other sensory types, showing cell-type-specific connectivity organized into micro-circuits with left-right symmetry (correlation=0.76).
results.evaluation: Claims C71-C78 provide detailed MB anatomy and connectivity. The classification into intrinsic and output neurons (C73) follows established MB nomenclature. The left-right correlation of 0.76 (C78) is lower than the whole-connectome value (0.91, C47) but still indicates substantial symmetry. The descriptions are consistent with prior partial reconstructions cited (C72).

results.result: The Platynereis mushroom body shows multilayer, parallel, feed-forward architecture with minimal recurrent connections and fan-out fan-in organization. This multilayer perceptron architecture may support associative memory formation.
results.evaluation: Claims C79-C80 describe the MB circuit architecture based on connectivity analysis. However, C81 is explicitly speculative ("may support") and cites comparative work in cephalopods rather than direct functional evidence in Platynereis. The architectural description is supported, but the functional interpretation requires experimental validation. The authors appropriately present this as a hypothesis.

results.result: Head-trunk connectivity involves 138 descending brain neurons and 75 ascending VNC neurons, with 549 trunk cells receiving head inputs and 288 head cells receiving trunk inputs. Trunk-projecting neurons have either decussating or ipsilaterally descending morphologies projecting to different VNC domains, receiving inputs in the head and forming outputs in the VNC.
results.evaluation: Claims C82-C86 quantify head-trunk connectivity with specific cell counts and anatomical descriptions. The segregation of decussating vs. descending neurons into different VNC domains (C85) and their input-output compartmentalization (C86) are based on direct anatomical observations with figure support.

results.result: The larval trunk comprises three chaetigerous segments plus a cryptic segment and pygidium, with ciliary bands marking segment boundaries. Connectivity analysis shows strongest within-segment connections but extensive intersegmental connectivity, with some neurons projecting along the entire body length. Different effector types show segment-specific innervation patterns.
results.evaluation: Claims C87-C96 describe segmental organization and intersegmental connectivity with citations to developmental studies (C87-C88). The connectivity patterns (C90-C96) are based on direct analysis of the connectome. The identification of neurons with "global reach" (C92) is a key finding enabled by whole-body reconstruction.

results.result: Segment-specific cell types reveal trunk heteromery: segment 1 contains 10 unique types including ciliomotor neurons, segment 2 has 8 types including giant MNspinning motoneurons innervating spinning glands, segment 3 has 2 types, and the pygidium has 7 types including pigment-motor neurons. These form unique segment-specific circuits.
results.evaluation: Claims C97-C104 document segment-specific cell types with specific counts and detailed circuit descriptions. The MNspinning-spinGland circuit (C99-C101) is particularly well-characterized anatomically. The pygidial pigment-motor neurons (C103-C104) represent a novel finding. The heteromeric organization is clearly demonstrated.

results.result: Several neuron types (chaeMech, INsplitPB, INbackcross, MNche, MNhose) occur in all chaetigerous segments, and four cell-type families (CR, PU, PB, INsplit) plus two muscle types occur across 5-6 body regions. This pattern may indicate serial homology suggesting metameric evolutionary origin for all body segments including head and pygidium.
results.evaluation: Claims C105-C106 document serially repeated cell types across segments with specific examples. The evolutionary interpretation (C107) is appropriately presented as inference ("may indicate") based on the anatomical pattern. The serial homology hypothesis is a reasonable interpretation of the data, though it requires comparative evidence for full support.

results.result: The mechanosensory girdle is an anatomically distinct system spanning the entire body with a circumoral ring continuing in two VNC tracts. It includes penetrating mechanosensory neurons (CR, PB, PU, interparaPM) with cilia surrounded by microvilli expressing polycystin mechanoreceptors, plus chaeMech chaetal mechanoreceptors.
results.evaluation: Claims C108-C112 describe a novel anatomical system with clear morphological criteria. The molecular characterization (C111) is supported by citations. The identification of this system as a distinct entity is justified by its anatomical coherence and shared molecular markers. The circumoral organization is particularly notable.

results.result: ChaeMech neurons are dendritic sensory cells in segments 1-3 with dendrites branching between chaetal sacs, potentially sensing chaetal displacement during crawling or external stimuli. They show similarities to bristle receptors in other annelids and dendritic proprioceptors in Drosophila, projecting to the VNC with mixed input-output compartments and connecting to premotor interneurons and motoneurons.
results.evaluation: Claims C113-C119 characterize chaeMech neurons anatomically and compare them to similar cells in other species (C115-C116). The functional speculation about proprioception (C114) is appropriately tentative. The comparative descriptions (C115-C117) are based on citations. The connectivity analysis (C118-C119) is directly supported by the connectome data.

results.result: ChaeMech neurons strongly innervate INsplitCR interneurons, which are also postsynaptic to collar receptors (CR) mediating startle responses. However, chaeMech and CR circuits are only partially overlapping, suggesting chaeMech may provide proprioceptive inhibitory feedback during startle through INsplitCR cells.
results.evaluation: Claims C120-C126 analyze the convergence and divergence of mechanosensory pathways. The connectivity patterns (C121-C125) are directly observed in the connectome. The functional hypothesis about proprioceptive feedback (C126) is appropriately presented as speculation ("suggests that there may be") based on the circuit architecture and cited functional studies of CR neurons (C122).

results.result: INsplit interneurons (pseudounipolar morphology) are the main postsynaptic partners of mechanosensory neurons, subdivided into distinct types (INsplitCR, INsplitPB, etc.) occurring across trunk segments and head with cell-type-specific connectivity. They are premotor neurons connecting to motoneurons innervating all effector types, thus mechanosensory neurons provide input to all body effector systems.
results.evaluation: Claims C127-C135 characterize the INsplit family comprehensively. The cell-type-specific connectivity patterns (C129-C132) are directly observed. The high network centrality (C133) is supported by graph analysis. The conclusion that mechanosensory input reaches all effector systems (C135) logically follows from the connectivity data (C134).

results.result: The authors reconstructed a whole-body connectome from a 3-day-old Platynereis larva using serial EM, identifying 9162 cells with somas and tracing 5.66 million nodes with ~28,000 pre- and postsynaptic sites, though ~15-19% of synaptic sites remained on unattached fragments.
results.evaluation: Reviewers describe this as 'an exceptional, high-quality and detailed description' and 'a wealth of high-quality data.' The reconstruction is characterized as 'painstakingly meticulous,' with no concerns raised about the completeness or quality of the dataset despite the presence of unattached fragments.

results.result: The Platynereis larval nervous system comprises an anterior brain connected to a paired ventral nerve cord (VNC) via circumesophageal connectives, with the trunk organized into five segments. Sensory neurons project ipsilaterally to ventro-lateral VNC bundles, interneurons have ipsi- or contralateral projections within the VNC neuropil, and motoneurons uniquely have peripheral projections with motor nerves concentrating dorsally.
results.evaluation: Reviewers acknowledge the work provides detailed anatomical descriptions and organization of the nervous system. The anatomical claims are part of the 'massive amount of high-quality data' that reviewers found convincing, with no specific critiques of these structural descriptions.

results.result: Neurons exhibit diverse morphological properties: median cable length of 97.1 µm (ranging to 1.2-1.7 mm for the largest neurons), median of 8 presynaptic and 6 postsynaptic sites (with largest neurons having >300 presynapses), and the ratio of pre- to postsynaptic sites distinguishes neuron classes. Most neurons are unipolar with <100 segments and lack primary cilia, though sensory neurons are bipolar with 0-5 sensory cilia.
results.evaluation: These morphological characterizations are part of the 'painstakingly meticulous' analysis praised by reviewers. The quantitative data and morphological descriptions are included in the 'wealth of data' that reviewers found to be of high quality, with no concerns raised about these measurements.

results.result: The synaptic connectome contains 2675 nodes connected by 14,066 directed edges formed by 26,881 synapses, forming a sparsely connected network (density 0.00197). Source nodes are predominantly sensory neurons, sink nodes are mostly effector cells, and the highest-degree nodes include ciliomotor neurons (Loop, Ser-tr1), sensory-motoneuron pygPBunp, and MNspinning.
results.evaluation: Reviewers describe the network analysis as part of the 'massive amount of high-quality data' and note the work provides detailed information about 'how sensory neurons, interneurons, motor neurons, and effector organs are connected.' No concerns were raised about the network statistics or connectivity patterns.

results.result: Community detection using the Leiden algorithm identified several functional modules in the connectome, including the anterior neurosecretory centre, mushroom bodies, visual circuit, ciliomotor network, mechanosensory modules, postural control module, and muscle-motor modules. Nodes within modules are more strongly interconnected than between modules, and several modules contain neurons previously shown to mediate specific behaviors.
results.evaluation: Reviewers note the work 'provides a wealth of data on cell type diversity and the modules that interconnect them' and will be useful for 'studies on cell type diversity, segmental vs. intersegmental connectivity, and mushroom bodies.' The modular organization is part of the accepted high-quality analysis.

results.result: The authors classified 966 neurons into 202 cell types (most represented by only 2 cells) and 3128 non-neuronal cells into 92 types, including diverse cell types such as epidermal, pigment, muscle, ciliated, glial, and gland cells. Developing structures (antennae, palps, stomodeum) contain immature sensory neurons with few synapses.
results.evaluation: Reviewers emphasize this work 'lays the foundations for studies on cell type diversity' and note the 'painstakingly meticulous' analysis. The comprehensive cell type classification is central to the paper's contribution and was not questioned by reviewers.

results.result: The cell-type connectome includes 84 sensory, 82 interneuron, 34 motoneuron, and 58 effector cell types, connected by 2410 edges formed by 14,640 synapses. Left-right connectivity shows high stereotypy (correlation 0.91), and network parameters are similar to C. elegans and C. intestinalis connectomes.
results.evaluation: Reviewers note this is 'only the third whole body connectome to be assembled' and provides 'a comparison with those less complex animals: the nematode Caenorhabditis elegans and the tunicate Ciona intestinalis.' The comparative analysis and stereotypy findings are accepted without critique.

results.result: Circuit analysis identified 4 sensory-motor neurons with direct motor output, 25 premotor sensory neurons, and a maximum of 5 hops from sensory neurons to effectors. 33 sensory neurons have no synaptic paths to effectors, of which 19 are neurosecretory cells with few synaptic partners.
results.evaluation: These circuit organization findings are part of the detailed connectivity analysis that reviewers found to be of high quality. The identification of different circuit motifs and path lengths contributes to understanding 'unimodal and multimodal sensory processing, and long-range and short-range connectivity' that reviewers noted.

results.result: Neurotransmitters or neuropeptides were assigned to 53 (26%) neuronal cell types, including 11 cholinergic, 3 serotonergic, 1 dopaminergic, 1 adrenergic, and 4 glutamatergic types, plus 38 cell types expressing one of 12 neuropeptides. 516 connectome neurons contained dense core vesicles indicative of peptidergic transmission.
results.evaluation: The molecular characterization is part of the comprehensive dataset that reviewers praised. While reviewers note the paper is 'burdensome to read and understand' due to its size, they do not question the validity of the molecular annotations provided.

results.result: The head contains 45 sensory neuron types and 52 head interneuron types, with information flowing from sensory clusters through interneurons to ciliomotor neurons, ventral motoneurons (vMNs), and descending interneurons. The vMNs form a postural control module that innervates contralateral muscles and ciliated cells. Several ciliomotor neurons directly innervate locomotor ciliary bands, and visual photoreceptors share postsynaptic interneurons with eyespot photoreceptors.
results.evaluation: Reviewers acknowledge the work provides detailed circuit-level analysis and will be useful to 'scientists interested in other nervous systems parts, their functions, and evolution.' The head circuit organization is part of the accepted high-quality data, with no specific concerns raised.

results.result: The mushroom bodies (MBs) comprise ventrolateral brain ganglia with sensory neurons (SNMB) and interneurons (INMB) classified into intrinsic and output projection types. MBs receive input from MB-intrinsic sensory neurons, antennae, palps, and other sensory types, with cell-type-specific connectivity organized into micro-circuits. The MB architecture is multilayer, parallel, and feed-forward with weak recurrent connections, showing left-right symmetry (correlation 0.76) and a fan-out fan-in organization that may support associative memory formation.
results.evaluation: Reviewers specifically note this work 'lays the foundations for studies on...mushroom bodies' and will be useful for scientists interested in these structures. The detailed MB analysis is part of the comprehensive dataset praised by reviewers, though one reviewer suggested 'there could be a single paper on the mushroom body' due to the depth of analysis.

results.result: Brain-trunk connectivity involves 138 descending brain neurons and 75 ascending VNC neurons, with 549 trunk cells receiving synapses from head neurons and 288 head cells receiving synapses from trunk neurons. Trunk-projecting brain neurons have either decussating or ipsilaterally descending morphology, projecting to different VNC domains with different targets, and receive most inputs in the central head neuropil while forming most presynapses in the VNC.
results.evaluation: This analysis of brain-trunk connectivity is part of the 'long-range and short-range connectivity' that reviewers noted the paper extracts. The detailed characterization of descending and ascending pathways is included in the accepted high-quality dataset.

results.result: The trunk comprises three chaetigerous segments plus a cryptic segment and pygidium, with ciliary bands marking segment boundaries. Connectivity analysis shows strongest connections within segments but also inter-segmental connections (except segment 0). Segment 1 interneurons connect to four other body regions, and the head, segment 1, and pygidium contain neurons with 'global reach' projecting along the entire body length. Different effector types receive innervation from specific segments.
results.evaluation: Reviewers note the work 'lays the foundations for studies on...segmental vs. intersegmental connectivity' and 'informs the understanding of the evolution of segmental body plans in annelids.' The segmental organization analysis is a key contribution that reviewers found valuable, though one suggested it could be a separate paper.

results.result: Segment-specific neuronal cell types include 10 in segment 1 (including ciliomotor neurons for body-wide ciliary control), 8 in segment 2 (including giant MNspinning motoneurons innervating contralateral spinning glands and forming reciprocal connections with INsplit interneurons), 2 in segment 3, and 7 in the pygidium (including motoneurons innervating head pigment cells). Several neuron types (chaeMech, INsplitPB, INbackcross, MNche, MNhose) occur in all chaetigerous segments.
results.evaluation: The detailed segment-specific cell type analysis is part of the comprehensive characterization that reviewers praised. This contributes to understanding 'the evolution of segmental body plans in annelids' that reviewers noted as a key finding.

results.result: Four cell-type families (CR, PU, PB, INsplit) and two muscle types (MUSlongV, MUStrans) occur across five or six body regions (head, segments 0-3, pygidium), a pattern that may indicate serial homology and suggest a metameric evolutionary origin for trunk segments, pygidium, and head.
results.evaluation: Reviewers note the work draws 'several interesting conclusions' including insights about evolution, specifically that 'circuit evolution might have proceeded by duplication and diversion of cell types.' This evolutionary inference from cell type distribution patterns is accepted as part of the paper's contributions.

results.result: Mechanosensory neurons and their postsynaptic partners form an anatomically distinct 'mechanosensory girdle' spanning the entire body, including penetrating collar receptor (CR), biciliated (PB), uniciliated (PU), and interparapodial multiciliated (interparaPM) neurons, all with penetrating sensory cilia surrounded by microvilli. CR and PB neurons express mechanosensory polycystins PKD2-1 (and PKD1-1 for CRs). The girdle also includes chaeMech dendritic cells that are chaetal mechanoreceptors.
results.evaluation: This identification of a body-wide mechanosensory system is part of the detailed circuit analysis that reviewers found to be of high quality. The mechanosensory girdle represents a novel organizational principle that contributes to understanding nervous system organization.

results.result: The chaeMech cells are dendritic sensory cells in segments 1-3 with dendrites branching between chaetal sacs, potentially sensing chaetal displacement during crawling (proprioception) or external stimuli. They are highly interconnected and project to the VNC where they synapse on premotor interneurons (INsplitCR, INsplitBronto, INchaeMech) and motoneurons (MNring, MNspinning). Their innervation of MNspinning suggests mechanosensation may regulate glandular secretion. The postsynaptic circuits of CRs and chaeMechs are only partially overlapping, with shared innervation of INsplitCR suggesting proprioceptive feedback during startle responses.
results.evaluation: The detailed analysis of chaeMech connectivity and function is part of the comprehensive circuit characterization that reviewers praised. The functional inferences about proprioception and feedback are supported by the connectivity data and comparative references, fitting within the accepted analytical framework.

results.result: The strongest postsynaptic partners of girdle mechanosensory neurons are ipsilateral INsplit interneurons with bifurcating projections, subdivided into distinct cell types (INsplitCR, INsplitPB, INsplitPBant, INsplitPB-RF/Ya, INsplitPUh, INsplitBronto, INCM) occurring in all four trunk segments and head with unique synaptic connectivity. Different mechanosensory types specifically target different INsplit subtypes. INsplitCR and INsplitPB are highly ranked by connectivity, suggesting integrating functions. INsplit neurons are premotor, connecting to trunk motoneurons that innervate glands, ciliated cells, muscles, and pigment cells, thus mechanosensory neurons provide input to all effector systems.
results.evaluation: This detailed characterization of the INsplit interneuron family and their role in mechanosensory processing is part of the comprehensive circuit analysis that reviewers found to be of high quality. The identification of cell-type-specific connectivity patterns contributes to understanding sensory processing organization.
